result:
No. Do not add Redis here.

The system has one writer, restores from SQLite on boot, and needs no cross-host coordination. Redis would add a failure domain (another process, network hop, persistence story to manage) without solving a constraint you actually have. If in-memory access speed becomes a bottleneck, the Elixir-native answers are ETS or a GenServer-held state, both of which stay inside the single process you already run.

Revisit only if one of those constraints changes: multiple writers, cross-host sharing, or a hot-path latency requirement SQLite can't meet.
